 1        A.     Technology Services Overview
 2   Q.   Please generally describe the Technology Services organization, and the work

 3        Technology Services performs to support SPS’s operations.

 4   A.   Technology Services performs Xcel Energy’s shared IT functions across all

 5        operating companies, including SPS. The key activities include enterprise

 6        application development and maintenance, foundational IT infrastructure

 7        management, systems controls for generation and grid operations, customer-facing

 8        technology platforms, cybersecurity protection, data center operations and

 9        architecture, and IT governance — all of which SPS requires to provide safe and

10        reliable electric service to its New Mexico customers.

11   Q.   What are the key drivers of Technology Services’ capital investment?

12   A.   There are five key drivers to IT investments: evolving cyber security threats,

13        replacing aging technology infrastructure, wildfire mitigation, evolving business

14        requirements, and grid modernization initiatives.

15   Q.   How does Technology Services determine when an existing application or

16        system needs to be replaced or upgraded?

17   A.   Technology Services works with each of the business areas and Operating

18        Companies to identify short and long-term technology needs. The needs typically


                                              11

                                      Direct Testimony
                                              of
                                     Megan N. Scheller

1         are greater than the organization’s ability to fund them, so Technology Services

2         evaluates and prioritizes any proposed Technology Services investment.

 3        Technology Services strives to achieve cost-effective technology investment by

 4        maintaining existing systems until the risks and/or costs associated with keeping

 5        aging technologies in place outweigh the benefits.

 6   Q.   How does Technology Services create their budget and prioritize investments?

 7   A.   Technology Services’ budget development, project prioritization, and project

 8        management leverages an established Technology Investment Governance (“TIG”)

 9        process. As part of the TIG process, key business and IT leaders are accountable

10        for managing demand intake, prioritization, and business outcomes of the IT

11        projects in their portfolios as they move from project inception towards in-service,

12        thereby ensuring that projects comply with IT portfolio and project management

13        requirements. TIG leadership is comprised of executive level and senior business

14        leaders in a partnership with IT leadership. IT works with each Business Area to

15        determine its specific IT needs, and needs are prioritized based on a particular set

16        of factors. Specifically, each Technology Services area is responsible for partnering

17        with a specific Business Area within the organization to determine that area’s long-

18        term strategic objectives and identify whether IT investments can enable


                                               12

                                  Megan N. Scheller

 1   achievement of those objectives. In turn, these priorities are converted into a

 2   proposed Technology Services budget. The TIG process also oversees and

 3   approves any changes in project scope or budget at the corporate level based on

 4   overall SPS priorities and spending levels.

 5           From the idea stage, project ideas are grouped and evaluated, ranked, and

 6   selected based on a common set of filters. This process weighs a multitude of

 7   criteria including: (1) the financial and non-financial benefits of a project, (2) the

 8   potential for other existing technologies to address the business need, and (3) the

 9   degree to which the project is needed to meet regulatory requirements or to ensure

10   system reliability and security. This categorization process allows Technology

11   Services to evaluate the benefits and risks associated with each project idea and

12   results in a list of ranked project ideas.

13           Under the TIG process, SPS reviews the ranked project ideas to determine

14   which projects should be implemented and included in the Technology Services

15   budget. This process requires further refinement of the budget figures for each

16   project and prioritization of possible projects until a final budget is set.

18        staffing, regulatory compliance, and any other benefits derived from the project.

13        requires reviews and approvals at the budget, management, senior management,

15        compare the monthly budget to actual expenditures. Accordingly, on a monthly

16        basis, Technology Services evaluates deviations to determine whether costs are

17        appropriate. In addition, Technology Services develops action plans to mitigate

18        variations in actual to budgeted expenditures. These mitigation plans may either

 4        B.     Enterprise Security Services (“ESS”) Overview
 5   Q.   Please describe ESS and the work they perform to support SPS’s operations.

 6   A.   ESS provides, maintains, and secures the properties and facilities that are used by

 7        SPS to serve its customers. The work performed in this category that is directly

 8        related to capital projects includes being responsible for implementation of physical

 9        security projects across all of Xcel Energy to monitor, detect, prevent, and

10        remediate unauthorized access to our physical infrastructure. Physical Security

11        involves costs associated with the physical security of employees, asset protection,

12        investigations, incident response and preparation to support Xcel Energy and SPS.

13        Examples include card readers, cameras, fencing, and access control equipment.

14        Capital additions are a necessary part of this work in order to provide safe, secure,

15        and compliant workspaces for employees and to protect the Company’s physical

16        infrastructure, which allows SPS to provide safe and reliable electric utility service

17        to SPS customers.

 3        within regulatory requirements governing the physical security of electrical

 4        facilities as well as ensuring the physical environment is secure from unwanted

 5        intrusions. These investments can take the form of physical assets such as cameras,

 6        card readers, and door locks. These investments also help the Company comply

 9   A.   For ESS, annually the team evaluates the need for future capital investment to

10        maintain and improve both our cyber and physical security environments. This

11        evaluation results in a list of prioritized projects for inclusion in the upcoming

12        capital budget. New items identified are categorized and prioritized along with

13        existing multi-year capital projects. Projects are reviewed against industry

14        standards, internal and external assessment results, and overall business need. The

15        final list of projects is also reviewed in consideration of overall Xcel Energy capital

16        guidelines.

 5        additions?

 7        the Protection Services team and area owners. Through a collaborative process, the

 8        scope is refined based on identification of the best technologies and systems that

 9        deliver what the team has determined necessary. Once the scope and technological

10        solution is clearly defined, ESS enlists its sole source vendor to physically walk the

11        facility and validate SPS’s scoping decisions. The vendor then develops a bid,

12        which our team inspects to make sure it meets the needs described in the scoping

13        process. The team also compares the proposed scope of work to other projects that

14        have been completed across the enterprise and in the industry as a check on the

15        reasonableness of the costs. Upon inspection, the quote is either rejected, modified,

16        or accepted.

 3   Q.     What do you mean when you refer to Technology and Security Services as a

 4          “cost center”?

 5   A.     The Future Test Period Rule defines the phrase “cost center” to mean the

 6          department, division, or organizational grouping of departments or divisions at

 7          which operating expense planning and evaluation takes place. 5 The Technology

 8          and Security Services organization within XES meets this definition.

 9   Q.     How are Technology Services and ESS – Physical Security related within the

10          organization?

11   A.     Technology Services and ESS – Physical Security are both departments within the
